cells.tense: You are holding what you have, and it is going out to people now.
cells.ask: Send one person the exact thing they need — the recipe, the form, the how-to — and stop there. Let the sending be the whole act, with nothing to maintain after.
cells.core:
There is something you carry that other people use, and right now it is moving out of your hands into theirs. You know what each person needs before they say it, and it goes where it should. That going-out is not a leak. It is what this strength does when it is working.

Where it can bend is at the edge: one thing handed over without checking that it fits the person, or one thing held back because handing it over felt like losing it. Neither is a crisis. Today, pass one thing along and watch what happens in the room without stepping back in. What you have is still yours while someone else uses it — the use is how it stays yours.
cells.sheetLine: Strength that goes out to people is still yours while they use it.
cells.verb: strength that leaves your hands and keeps working in other people's
cells.place: in what gets said and passed along between people, the part that outlives the moment

cells.tense: You will have them covered before they ever think to ask you.
cells.ask: Notice the first need you feel forming on someone's behalf today, then wait one minute. If it is still there after they ask, help then — not before.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead of this hour, someone is going to need something, and you are already arranging it — the favor lined up, the ride sorted, the answer drafted. The strength under that is real. What is new is the bracing. You are answering a need that has not arrived, so your help gets there before the person does.

In that hurry, what you hand over can stop being exchange and start being management. Giving only what was asked for is not giving less; it is handing over the thing itself instead of your plan for it. There is a balance here worth keeping: what you have flows, and what you keep for yourself is not a betrayal of the flow. Let one need belong to its owner today and see if anything is lost.

cells.tense: You used to hand things to people, and the handing stopped.
cells.ask: Tell one person something you know — how to fix it, how to word it, how to cook it — and let them take it without you following up. Offer and be done.
cells.core:
What you know is still in you, and so is what you have. What is quiet is the offering. Where you would once have passed it along without a second thought, now the second thought arrives first and nothing leaves your hands.

Closing off worked in its way. You kept what was yours. But the same closed hands keep it from the people standing in front of you who could use it, and the waiting has gotten heavy. You do not need the reason for the closing to start again. One thing you know, handed to one person, with nothing asked in return. The person can take it or leave it. Either way the hands are open.

cells.tense: You are keeping this alive for the people around you while calling it nobody's in particular.
cells.ask: Name one piece of shared ground — a saying, a ritual, a way your people do things — and say out loud, once, where it came from and that you kept it going.
cells.core:
Look at what stays alive among the people around you — the phrases, the rituals, the way a bad week gets handled. You are the one holding those up. You decide what still counts, you adjust it, you pass it to whoever is standing there. That has been going on for a while.

When you describe it, though, it sounds like the thing runs on its own and you happen to be nearby. The work is real; the saying-so is not happening, and the saying-so is what protects it when it gets tested. Nothing needs defending here. It needs the same plain honesty you would give anything else you built. Say one piece of it is yours, and see that the sharing does not break.
cells.sheetLine: You're already keeping this alive. Naming it yours doesn't end it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim I could slide into is that Support gone Too Much means the person is over-giving — saving people, over-supporting family, giving resources away — when the record only says the strength is turned outward past the point where it can hold, which can look like holding too much or holding too hard. The reader could reasonably say it is simply grief, or a busy month, or that none of this is about holding. The asks survive being wrong: each is a small physical act, doable today, and useful even if the reading misses — a visiting, a feed, a choosing, a naming. The sentence that serves me more than the person is anything like 'your strength is a gift others depend on,' which flatters the card and tells them nothing.
